sakt-p01-v01.quick_english: Place, entry, form, and mark and sign indeed; raising, awakening, and wheel-rest indeed — and.

sakt-p01-v02.quick_english: Stage-arrival and indeed final state so indeed; rest, transformation and, so-returning indeed — and.

sakt-p01-v03.quick_english: Thus thirteenfold Śākta supreme-knowledge; in all Trika treatises indicated by Śambhu himself.

sakt-p01-v04.quick_english: Below navel fingers five, above the member two fingers; in that middle, bulb-named, and wheel-place thus remembered.

sakt-p01-v05.quick_english: By breath-restraint mind right there should cast; fully conquering wind-course, until to middle-going lead.

sakt-p01-v06.quick_english: This entry, thus they call; form I will tell now: triangle-pond-like wheel, six-spoked, and further firm.

sakt-p01-v07.quick_english: Pomegranate-blossom-like bulb, indeed naturally red; this form declared third, consisting of contemplation.

sakt-p01-v08.quick_english: In that middle should place mind, until there made steady; having left obstruction, when wind — then mark point out.

sakt-p01-v09.quick_english: Of bulb-wheel standing in middle — but consisting-of-unstruck digit; below-above line-joined, serpent-coiled-shaped.

sakt-p01-v10.quick_english: Up-down abiding-state, sun and moon both; truly shining forth she, thousand-sun-equal-radiance.

sakt-p02-v11.quick_english: Her indeed should gaze — śakti — slightly by kumbhaka-mode; this sign pointed out, raising beyond from here.

sakt-p02-v12.quick_english: By practised-exhale-mode but mantra and indeed should utter; awakened should contemplate śakti, staff-like supreme goddess.

sakt-p02-v13.quick_english: Come from base-middle, suṣumnā-path resorted to; raising declared, awakening beyond thus.

sakt-p02-v14.quick_english: Standing in bulb should pierce navel, then standing in heart grandsire; standing in throat unfallen, Rudra face to face, on palate-surface standing.

sakt-p02-v15.quick_english: Gone to brow-middle but Īśa, at brahma-door Sadāśiva; having awakened should go swiftly to state, and unsupported Śiva.

sakt-p02-v16.quick_english: This awakening pointed out; wheel-resting then: natural petal, blazing, flowing, steady-sky-like.

sakt-p02-v17.quick_english: Nectar, crest, and indeed śakti-brahmā so indeed and; drop-sound thus proclaimed, twelvefold-wheel — tradition says.

sakt-p02-v18.quick_english: Piercing in order — śakti in wheel, in wheel each moment; should rest she great goddess: wheel-rest supreme.

sakt-p02-v19.quick_english: Heart trembles first, palate-gate indeed and; head and whirls of him: sight-transmission sign.

sakt-p02-v20.quick_english: Each single causes to whirl — limb — in limb-sub-limb joints; swirls heart and of him by true-knowledge power.

sakt-p03-v21.quick_english: Whatever whatever changes state makes of being; in those in those not to be feared — plays supreme goddess.

sakt-p03-v22.quick_english: In nectar she this intoxicated, changes makes many; triple-stain-changes, in many births what done —

sakt-p03-v23.quick_english: Shakes off stained ones from bond, arisen from supreme power; stage-arrival proclaimed, final state thus is told.

sakt-p03-v24.quick_english: When at transmission: hair-thrill, tear-fall, yawn-onset, faltering speech of voices within; knot-bursting, touch-divine-thrill, drop-throbbings from navel-bulb throb forth.

sakt-p03-v25.quick_english: Final state declared; rest but now is told: come forth from navel-wheel when śakti awakens.

sakt-p03-v26.quick_english: Then but set: whole sense-host outside standing; when she supreme power well dissolved in supreme state.

sakt-p03-v27.quick_english: Then not finds anything — subject other object; in Śiva is rested śakti then: rest is called.

sakt-p03-v28.quick_english: Where resting — of śakti mind there — to dissolution should go; then self in supreme-selfness to be known by firm-souled ones.

sakt-p03-v29.quick_english: Become Śiva becomes self: transformation that indeed for; always he rains divine nectar, creature-life.

sakt-p03-v30.quick_english: Mind there but having held, again goddess should enter she; then but return proclaimed thus: fully thirteen.

sakt-p01-v01.inference: The thirteen-member Śākta doctrine is complete and Trika-scriptural, revealed by Śambhu himself.
premises: Thirteen named members: place, entry, form, mark, sign, raising, awakening, wheel-rest, stage-arrival, final state, rest, transformation, return.
The whole set is one supreme esoteric doctrine (vijñāna, sdv), not thirteen separate techniques.
Every Trika treatise carries it by Śambhu's own indication — lineage authority closes the list.
sakt-p01-v01.question: What is the Śākta doctrine?
sakt-p01-v01.speaker: Teacher (enumerating)

sakt-p01-v02.inference: The ascent continues through rest, transformation, and return — the list is a closed thirteen.
premises: Second list-half: stage-arrival, final state, rest, transformation, return.
Verse-closing ca members bind vv1-2 into one thirteenfold sentence.
Nothing outside the thirteen belongs to the doctrine.
sakt-p01-v02.question: What completes the thirteen?
sakt-p01-v02.speaker: Teacher (enumerating)

sakt-p01-v03.inference: The doctrine's authority is direct revelation, hence supreme.
premises: Thirteenfold, Śākta, supreme knowledge: three predicates of one vijñāna.
Indicated in all Trika treatises — ubiquity across the corpus.
By Śambhu himself — no intermediary lineage dilutes the claim.
sakt-p01-v03.question: Why supreme?
sakt-p01-v03.speaker: Teacher (authorizing)

sakt-p01-v10.speaker: Teacher (praising)

sakt-p02-v11.inference: Gazing at her with light breath-hold defines the sign; raising begins beyond it.
premises: Act: gaze at śakti with slight kumbhaka-mode.
Formula: this is the sign pointed out.
Sequence: from here, raising lies beyond.
sakt-p02-v11.question: How is the sign observed?
sakt-p02-v11.speaker: Teacher (instructing)

sakt-p02-v12.inference: On the exhale utter mantra and contemplate her awakened, risen rod-straight as Supreme Goddess.

option_choices.reason: Staff-erect (risen straight like a stick) fits the raising action of vv12-13; a prostrate reading contradicts the upward movement the verse enacts.

premises: Breath: practised exhale-mode carries the utterance.
Speech: mantra uttered on the exhale.
Vision: śakti contemplated as already awakened, staff-straight, Supreme Goddess.
sakt-p02-v12.question: How is she raised?
sakt-p02-v12.speaker: Teacher (instructing)

sakt-p02-v13.inference: Raising is declared in her path from base to channel; awakening lies beyond.
premises: Path: come from the base-middle, resorted to the suṣumnā.
Closure: raising is declared (sixth member complete).
Opening: awakening beyond thus (seventh member announced).
sakt-p02-v13.question: Where does raising end?
sakt-p02-v13.speaker: Teacher (sealing)

sakt-p02-v14.inference: Awakening pierces upward station by station: navel, heart, throat, palate.
premises: Start: standing in the bulb, pierce the navel.
Middle: then the heart-dwelling grandsire.
Crown of the verse: throat-dwelling unfallen, Rudra face to face on the palate-surface.
sakt-p02-v14.question: What does the piercing climb?
sakt-p02-v14.speaker: Teacher (climbing)

sakt-p02-v15.inference: The climb ends past brow and brahma-door in the unsupported Śiva state.
premises: Brow: gone to the brow-middle — Īśa.
Door: at the brahma-door — Sadāśiva.
Flight: having awakened them, go swiftly to the unsupported Śiva state.
sakt-p02-v15.question: Where does the climb arrive?
sakt-p02-v15.speaker: Teacher (arriving)

sakt-p02-v16.inference: Awakening closed; wheel-resting opens as natural, blazing, flowing, sky-steady.
premises: Seal: this awakening is pointed out (seventh member complete).
Opening: wheel-resting then (eighth member announced).
Texture: natural petal, blazing, flowing, like the steady sky.
sakt-p02-v16.question: What is wheel-rest like?
sakt-p02-v16.speaker: Teacher (resting)

sakt-p02-v17.inference: The wheel is twelvefold, proclaimed by tradition — nectar, crest, śakti-brahmā, drop-sound among its names.

option_choices.reason: One compound name (śakti-brahmā) keeps the accusative name-list syntax intact; a copular split ('śakti is Brahmā') breaks the list the verse is enumerating.

premises: Names: nectar, crest, śakti-brahmā, drop-sound — members of the twelve.
Proclamation: thus proclaimed (received formula).
Attribution: tradition says (kila) — doctrine received, not invented.
sakt-p02-v17.question: How many wheels?
sakt-p02-v17.speaker: Teacher (counting)

sakt-p02-v18.inference: She pierces in order and rests in every wheel, each moment — that rest is supreme.
premises: Agency: she pierces, in order, wheel in wheel.
Tempo: each moment — no wheel skipped, no pause.
Fruit: she, the Great Goddess, should rest — wheel-rest supreme.
sakt-p02-v18.question: Who rests in the wheels?
sakt-p02-v18.speaker: Teacher (beholding)

sakt-p02-v19.inference: The stage-signs begin in the body: trembling heart, palate gate, whirling head — the mark of sight-transmission.
premises: Heart trembles first — priority of the cardiac sign.
Palate-gate joins it; the head whirls.
The three together are the sign of sight-transmission (Timirodghāṭana term, sdv).
sakt-p02-v19.question: What are the first signs?
sakt-p02-v19.speaker: Teacher (diagnosing)

sakt-p02-v20.inference: True knowledge whirls every limb in its joints; his heart swirls by that power.
premises: Scope: each single limb, down to limb-sub-limb joints.
Agent: the power of true vidyā (causative kept — she whirls, limbs are whirled).
Intensification: the heart swirls — trembling grown into churning.
sakt-p02-v20.question: How far does the whirling go?
sakt-p02-v20.speaker: Teacher (diagnosing)

sakt-p03-v21.inference: No produced change is to be feared, because the Supreme Goddess plays.
premises: Whatever changes the state makes in a being — total scope, doubled.
In those very changes: no fear (gerundive of fearlessness).
Ground: she plays — her play (krīḍā) is the fear's antidote, not its cause.
sakt-p03-v21.question: Must the changes be feared?
sakt-p03-v21.speaker: Teacher (reassuring)

sakt-p03-v22.inference: Drunk on nectar she multiplies changes — the residue of many births' stained doing.

option_choices.reason: Staying with the GRETIL surface (triple-stain changes) refuses an emendation; the -eṇa instrumental reading is recorded but would rewrite the witness against its bytes.

premises: State: intoxicated in nectar — her unmattā as method, not lapse.
Act: she makes many changes (the vidyā-power churning of v20 continued).
Material: what was done in many births under the triple stain.
sakt-p03-v22.question: Why do the changes multiply?
sakt-p03-v22.speaker: Teacher (explaining)

sakt-p03-v23.inference: She shakes the stained ones off from bondage — that is stage-arrival; the final state is told next.
premises: Liberation: shakes off the stained ones from the bond.
Agency: arisen from the supreme power (her own source).
Seal and pivot: stage-arrival proclaimed; final state thus told.
sakt-p03-v23.question: What does the shaking accomplish?
sakt-p03-v23.speaker: Teacher (sealing)

sakt-p03-v24.inference: At transmission the body testifies: thrill, tears, yawning, faltering voice, burst knots, throbbing drops from the navel bulb.
premises: Onset signs: hair-thrill, tear-fall, yawn-onset, faltering speech within.
Deep signs: knot-bursting, divine thrill of touch.
Crown sign: drop-throbbings throb forth from the navel bulb (plural verb — many drops).
sakt-p03-v24.question: How does transmission feel?
sakt-p03-v24.speaker: Teacher (witnessing)
uncertainties: giro 'ntaḥ parsing ('of voices within') stays literal and uncertain — flagged, not smoothed.

sakt-p03-v25.inference: That is the final state declared; and rest is told next, when śakti wakes from the navel wheel.
premises: The yat of v24 resolves here: the sign-list was the final state.
Declared (seal of the tenth member).
Pivot: rest (eleventh) is told next, conditioned on her awakening from the navel wheel.
sakt-p03-v25.question: What was all that?
sakt-p03-v25.speaker: Teacher (naming)

sakt-p03-v26.inference: In repose the whole outer sense-host sets; she lies well dissolved in the supreme state.
premises: Setting: the whole sense-village stands set outside (like the sun gone down).
Condition: when she, the supreme power, is well dissolved.
Locus: in the supreme state (dissolution, not sleep).
sakt-p03-v26.question: What sets in repose?
sakt-p03-v26.speaker: Teacher (describing)

sakt-p03-v27.inference: The subject finds no other object; rested in Śiva is śakti — that is called rest.
premises: Negation: the subject finds nothing, no other object (ellipsis kept).
Union: in Śiva she is rested (passive — she is rested, not rests).
Naming: śakti-then is rest called (eleventh member sealed).
sakt-p03-v27.question: What is rest?
sakt-p03-v27.speaker: Teacher (defining)

sakt-p03-v28.inference: Where her resting is, there the mind should dissolve; the self is then known in supreme-selfness by the firm-souled.
premises: Locus: where the resting of śakti is, there the mind.
Act: should go to dissolution (optative prescription).
Fruit: the self is to be known in supreme-selfness — by the firm-souled (not by all).
sakt-p03-v28.question: Where should the mind go?
sakt-p03-v28.speaker: Teacher (directing)

sakt-p03-v29.inference: Become-Śiva is the self — that is transformation; and he rains divine nectar, creature-life.
premises: Thesis: become Śiva, the self becomes (the work's pivot sentence).
Naming: that indeed is transformation (twelfth member sealed).
Overflow: always he rains divine nectar — and the nectar is creature-life.
sakt-p03-v29.question: What is transformation?
sakt-p03-v29.speaker: Teacher (proclaiming)

sakt-p03-v30.inference: Mind held there, the goddess re-enters — that return, fully thirteen, closes the doctrine.
premises: Preparation: mind held there (gerund prior act).
Return: the goddess again should enter — she re-enters (āgamana enacted).
Closure: return proclaimed thus — fully thirteen (the v3 iti frame sealed).
sakt-p03-v30.question: How does the doctrine close?
sakt-p03-v30.speaker: Teacher (closing)

sakt-p01-v01.plain_english: Place, entry, form, and mark, and sign indeed; raising, awakening, and wheel-rest indeed — and
sakt-p01-v01.sanskrit_cite: sthānaṃ praveśo rūpaṃ ca lakṣaṃ lakṣaṇameva ca / utthāpanaṃ bodhanaṃ ca cakraviśrāmameva ca

sakt-p01-v02.plain_english: the arrival at the stage, and the final state indeed; rest, transformation, and the return indeed — and
sakt-p01-v02.sanskrit_cite: bhūmikāgamanaṃ caiva antāvasthā tathaiva ca / viśrāmaḥ pariṇāmaśca tathāgamanameva ca

sakt-p01-v03.plain_english: So the doctrine is thirteenfold: the supreme Śākta wisdom, pointed out in every Trika treatise by Śambhu himself.
sakt-p01-v03.sanskrit_cite: iti trayodaśavidhaṃ śāktaṃ vijñānamuttamam / sarveṣu trikaśāstreṣu sūcitaṃ śambhunā svayam

sakt-p01-v04.plain_english: Five fingers below the navel, two fingers above the member — between them lies the place called the bulb, remembered as the station of the wheel.
sakt-p01-v04.sanskrit_cite: nābhyadho 'ṅgulāḥ pañca meḍhrasyordhvāṅguladvayam / tanmadhye kandanāmā ca cakrasthānamiti smṛtam

sakt-p01-v05.plain_english: Hold the breath in and out, and cast the mind right there; master the currents of wind completely, and lead them until they enter the middle.
sakt-p01-v05.sanskrit_cite: prāṇāpānanirodhena manastatraiva niḥkṣipet / samyag vāyugatiṃ jitvā yāvan madhyagatāṃ nayet

sakt-p01-v06.plain_english: This — they say — is entry. Now I will tell the form: a wheel like a horned pond, six-spoked, and steady beyond.
sakt-p01-v06.sanskrit_cite: eṣa praveśa ity āhū rūpaṃ vakṣyāmi cādhunā / śṛṅgāṭakanibhaṃ cakraṃ ṣaḍaraṃ cāparaṃ dhruvam

sakt-p01-v07.plain_english: The bulb glows like a pomegranate blossom, red by its very nature; this form is declared the third — it consists of contemplation.
sakt-p01-v07.sanskrit_cite: dāḍimīkusumaprakhyaṃ kandaṃ vai jātilohitam / etadrūpaṃ samākhyātaṃ tṛtīyaṃ cintanātmakam

sakt-p01-v08.plain_english: Set the mind in that middle until it stands steady there; when the wind's hold is released, point out the mark.
sakt-p01-v08.sanskrit_cite: tanmadhye nikṣipec cittaṃ yāvat tatra sthirīkṛtam / tyaktaruddho yadā vāyustadā lakṣaṃ vinirdiśet

sakt-p01-v09.plain_english: In the middle of the bulb-wheel stands a digit of the unstruck sound, ringed with lines above and below, coiled like a serpent.
sakt-p01-v09.sanskrit_cite: kandacakrasya madhyasthā tv anāhatamayī kalā / adhaūrdhve rekhāsaṃyuktā bhujaṃgakuṭilākṛtiḥ

sakt-p01-v10.plain_english: Above and below abides her state — sun and moon both; truly she shines, bright as a thousand suns.
sakt-p01-v10.sanskrit_cite: ūrdhvādho 'vasthitāvasthā sūryācandramasāv ubhau / satyaṃ virājamānā sā sahasrārkasamaprabhā

sakt-p02-v11.plain_english: Gaze at her, at śakti, with a light sealing of the breath; this is the sign pointed out — beyond it lies raising.
sakt-p02-v11.sanskrit_cite: tāmevālokayec chaktiṃ manāk kumbhakavṛttinā / etal lakṣaṇam uddiṣṭam utthāpanam ataḥ param

sakt-p02-v12.plain_english: On the practiced out-breath, utter the mantra; contemplate her awakened — the Supreme Goddess, straight as a staff.
sakt-p02-v12.sanskrit_cite: juṣadrecakavṛttyā tu mantraṃ caiva samuccaret / prabuddhāṃ cintayecchaktiṃ daṇḍavat parameśvarīm

sakt-p02-v13.plain_english: Come from the heart of the base, she has entered the suṣumnā road; this is raising declared — beyond it, awakening.
sakt-p02-v13.sanskrit_cite: ādhāramadhyādāyātā suṣumnāmārgam āśritā / utthāpanaṃ samākhyātaṃ bodhanaṃ paratastathā

sakt-p02-v14.plain_english: Rooted in the bulb, pierce the navel, then the grandsire in the heart; in the throat the unfallen one, Rudra face to face on the palate's floor.
sakt-p02-v14.sanskrit_cite: kandastho vedhayen nābhiṃ tato hṛtsthaṃ pitāmaham / kaṇṭhasthamacyutaṃ sākṣādrudraṃ tālutale sthitam

sakt-p02-v15.plain_english: At the brow's middle, Īśa; at the door of brahman, Sadāśiva; wake them and rise swiftly to the state that rests on nothing — Śiva.
sakt-p02-v15.sanskrit_cite: bhruvormadhyagataṃ tv īśaṃ brahmadvāre sadāśivam / bodhayitvā vrajed āśu padaṃ cānāśritaṃ śivam

sakt-p02-v16.plain_english: This awakening is pointed out. Then the resting in the wheels: a petal by nature, blazing, flowing, like the steady sky.
sakt-p02-v16.sanskrit_cite: etadbodhanam uddiṣṭaṃ cakraviśrāmaṇaṃ tataḥ / svābhāvikaṃ dalaṃ dīptaṃ dravaṃ sthiranabhopamam

sakt-p02-v17.plain_english: Nectar, the crest, śakti-brahmā — and the drop-sound: so the twelvefold wheel is proclaimed, says tradition.
sakt-p02-v17.sanskrit_cite: amṛtaṃ śekharaṃ caiva śaktirbrahmā tathaiva ca / bindunādaṃ tathā proktaṃ cakradvādaśakaṃ kila

sakt-p02-v18.plain_english: Piercing in turn — śakti in wheel after wheel, at every instant — she, the Great Goddess, comes to rest: the supreme wheel-rest.
sakt-p02-v18.sanskrit_cite: vedhayantī kramāc chaktiścakre cakre pratikṣaṇam / viśramet sā mahādevī cakraviśrāma uttamaḥ

sakt-p02-v19.plain_english: First the heart trembles, and the palate gate; his head spins — the sign of the sight's crossing over.
sakt-p02-v19.sanskrit_cite: hṛdayaṃ kampate pūrvaṃ tālukadvārameva ca / śiraśca bhramate tasya dṛṣṭisaṃkrāntilakṣaṇam

sakt-p02-v20.plain_english: It sets each limb spinning, joint by joint; his heart churns — such is the power of true knowing.
sakt-p02-v20.sanskrit_cite: ekaikaṃ bhramayaty aṅgam aṅgapratyaṅgasaṃdhiṣu / ghūrṇate hṛdayaṃ cāsya samyagvidyāprabhāvataḥ

sakt-p03-v21.plain_english: Whatever changes the state brews in a man — in none of them is there anything to fear; the Supreme Goddess is at play.
sakt-p03-v21.sanskrit_cite: yāni yāni vikārāṇi avasthā kurute sataḥ / teṣu teṣu na bhetavyaṃ krīḍati parameśvarī

sakt-p03-v22.plain_english: Drunk on nectar, she brews change upon change — the triple-stain ferment of what was done through many births.
sakt-p03-v22.sanskrit_cite: amṛte seyam unmattā vikārān kurute bahūn / malatrayavikārau bahujanmasu yatkṛtam

sakt-p03-v23.plain_english: She shakes the stained souls loose from the snare, risen from supreme power; this is the arrival at the stage — and the final state is told.
sakt-p03-v23.sanskrit_cite: dhunoti samalān pāśāt paraśaktisamutthitān / bhūmikāgamanaṃ proktam antāvasthā tathocyate

sakt-p03-v24.plain_english: When the crossing comes: hair rising, tears falling, yawning breaking, speech faltering from voices within; knots bursting, the divine shiver of touch, drops throbbing out from the navel bulb.
sakt-p03-v24.sanskrit_cite: yat saṃkrāntau romaharṣo 'srupāto jṛmbhārambho gadgadā gīr giro 'ntaḥ / granthisphoṭaḥ sparśadivyapraharṣo binduspandā nābhikandāt sphuranti

sakt-p03-v25.plain_english: That is the final state declared. And now rest is taught: when śakti wakes and pours from the navel wheel.
sakt-p03-v25.sanskrit_cite: antāvasthā samākhyātā viśrāmas tv adhunocyate / nābhicakraviniryātā yadā śaktiḥ prabudhyate

sakt-p03-v26.plain_english: Then the whole village of the senses sets and stands without; when she, the supreme power, dissolves into the supreme place.
sakt-p03-v26.sanskrit_cite: tadā tv astamitaṃ sarvamakṣagrāmaṃ bahiḥ sthitam / yadā sā paramā śaktiḥ sulīnā parame pade

sakt-p03-v27.plain_english: Then the knower finds nothing — no other thing to know; śakti rests in Śiva — this is called rest.
sakt-p03-v27.sanskrit_cite: tadā na vindate kiṃcid viṣayī viṣayāntaram / śive viśrāmyate śaktistadā viśrāma ucyate

sakt-p03-v28.plain_english: Where her resting lies, let the mind go there into dissolution; then the self is known in supreme selfhood by those made firm.
sakt-p03-v28.sanskrit_cite: yatra viśramaṇaṃ śaktermanastatra layaṃ vrajet / tadātmā paramātmatve jñātavyo niścitātmabhiḥ

sakt-p03-v29.plain_english: Become Śiva — the self turns Śiva; that indeed is the turning. And he rains forever the divine nectar that is the life of creatures.
sakt-p03-v29.sanskrit_cite: śivībhūto bhavatyātmā pariṇāmaḥ sa eva hi / sadā sa varṣate divyam amṛtaṃ jantujīvanam

sakt-p03-v30.plain_english: Hold the mind there — and the goddess enters again; then the return is proclaimed: thirteen in full.
sakt-p03-v30.sanskrit_cite: cittaṃ tatra tu saṃdhārya punardaivī viśettu sā / tadā tv āgamanaṃ proktamevaṃ samyak trayodaśa

essence: Thirteen members named: the whole Śākta doctrine held in one breath.
Rest, transformation, return: thirteen members, nothing outside.
Supreme wisdom revealed by Śambhu himself across every Trika treatise.
The bulb's site measured: five below the navel, two above — the wheel's station.
Breath held, mind cast there, winds mastered into the middle — that is entry.
Entry sealed by custom; the form shown: horned-pond wheel, six spokes, firm.
Pomegranate-red bulb, third member — form as contemplation itself.
Mind steadied in the middle, obstruction gone — then the mark is given.
The unstruck digit mid-wheel, line-bound, serpent-coiled — the sign.
Her abiding spans high and low, sun and moon, thousand-sun bright.

rasa.dominant: adbhuta with vīra-utsāha (wonder braced by resolve)
rasa.justification: Wonder at the body revealed as doctrine — measured bulb, red wheel, serpent-coiled digit, thousand-sun radiance; the optative prescriptions (cast, lead, place, point out) summon the practitioner's resolve inside the wonder.

sections.BOUNDARY: No piercing happens here, no trembling, no rest. The ladder, the signs, and the repose belong to members pledged but not yet paid.
sections.EXPLANATION: The thirteen divide into naming and enacting: vv1-3 count the members whole, vv4-10 walk the first five in the body. Sthāna is found by measure, praveśa by breath-restraint and mind cast exactly, rūpa by teacher-shown vision (a firm six-spoked wheel), lakṣa by steadied mind meeting handled wind, lakṣaṇa by gazing at the serpent-coiled unstruck digit. Vijñāna here means the esoteric doctrine itself (sdv), and śākta carries its Kaula weight.
sections.FUNCTION: Lays measurable ground for the ascent and seals it with revealed authority, so every later tremor and rest already owns its place in a counted whole.
sections.KEY TERMS: sthāna (standing place) — the kanda found by finger-measure; praveśa (entry) — breath restrained, mind cast, wind led middle-ward; rūpa (form) — the seen wheel, consisting of contemplation (cintanātmaka); lakṣa (mark) — the assigned focus, distinct from the sign; lakṣaṇa (sign) — the observed unstruck digit; kanda (bulb) — pomegranate-red, six-spoked station; vijñāna (esoteric doctrine) — supreme thirteenfold knowledge.
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: All thirteen members pledged at the opening govern the whole work; raising through return, enacted beyond, are already owed by the list.
sections.RELATED: Trika treatises as the doctrine's carriers (v3); śākta as kaula (sdv) — the Kuṇḍalinī frame present though the name never sounds; Mahānaya thirteenfold table as the ready gloss bank.
sections.SUMMARY: Thirteen members hold the Śākta wisdom entire, from the bulb's measured site to the thousand-sun radiance of the Goddess. Breath restrained and mind fixed, entry opens; a six-spoked wheel appears, pomegranate-red; the unstruck digit coils serpent-like at the wheel's heart. Naming becomes seeing: the counted doctrine already glows in the body.

essence: Sealed breath, steady gaze at śakti — the sign defined, raising beyond.
Mantra on the exhale; her contemplated awakened, straight as a staff.
From the base-middle into the suṣumnā road — raising declared, awakening beyond.
Bulb-rooted piercing: navel, heart-grandsire, throat-unfallen, palate Rudra.
Brow-Īśa, brahma-door Sadāśiva — wakened, then flight to unsupported Śiva.
Awakening sealed; wheel-resting: petal, blaze, flow, steady sky.
Nectar, crest, śakti-brahmā, drop-sound — the twelvefold wheel proclaimed.
She pierces in order, rests wheel by wheel each moment — supreme wheel-rest.
Heart trembles first, palate gate, head whirls — sight-transmission's sign.
Limb by limb the whirling spreads through the joints; the heart churns by true knowing.

rasa.dominant: adbhuta strained toward bhayānaka (wonder edged with fear)
rasa.justification: The visions thrill — staff-straight Goddess, deity-ladder climbed, Great Goddess resting wheel by wheel — and then the body itself trembles, whirls, churns. Fear lives in the limbs before any verse refuses it; wonder carries a pulse of dread.

sections.BOUNDARY: Fear is read but not yet refused; the refusal (not to be feared) belongs ahead. The signs here are diagnosed as progress, not stilled into rest — stilling belongs to repose.
sections.EXPLANATION: Raising rides the exhale: mantra uttered, śakti seen already awakened and rod-straight. Awakening climbs a deity-ladder — navel, grandsire of the heart, unfallen of the throat, Rudra face to face on the palate, Īśa at the brow, Sadāśiva at the brahma-door — and exits into the unsupported. Wheel-resting is textured (petal, blaze, flow, steady sky) and counted (twelvefold, by tradition). Then the ninth member breaks into the body: trembling, whirling, joint-by-joint churning, all by true knowledge's power — with the Timirodghāṭana term sight-transmission naming the event.
sections.FUNCTION: Turns map into motion: prescribes the raising acts, then reads the body's answer as confirmation — so trembling registers as arrival, not disturbance.
sections.KEY TERMS: utthāpana (raising) — exhale, mantra, staff-straight vision; bodhana (awakening) — the pierced ladder to the unsupported; cakraviśrāma (wheel-resting) — pierced in order, rested in each wheel; daṇḍavat (staff-like) — risen straight, not prostrate; kumbhaka (sealing) — the light breath-hold of gazing; dṛṣṭisaṃkrānti (sight-transmission) — the Timirodghāṭana name for the signs.
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: The sixth through eighth members pledged at the opening are paid here in acts; the ninth breaks in early, its signs already shaking the body before its own section.
sections.RELATED: Timirodghāṭana as the quoted source of the sign-verses (sdv); the suṣumnā road as the climbed channel; Kaula antiquity grounding the practice's age.
sections.SUMMARY: Sealed breath finds her; mantra rides the exhale and she stands awakened, straight as a staff. The climb pierces navel, heart, throat, palate, brow, and crown-door, then rests wheel by wheel through a twelvefold round. And the body answers — trembling heart, whirling head, limbs spun joint by joint in the power of true knowing.

essence: Whatever the state brews — in none of it anything to fear; the Goddess plays.
Nectar-drunk she multiplies changes: many births' stained doing fermented.
The stained shaken off the snare, supreme-powered — stage-arrival sealed.
Transmission's body-signature: thrill, tears, yawning, faltering inner voices.
Knots burst, touch turns divine, drops throb from the navel bulb.
The sign-list resolves: final state declared; rest taught next.
Senses set without, she dissolved in the supreme — that is repose's ground.
Subject finds nothing, no other object; rested in Śiva — rest named.
Mind to dissolution where her resting lies; self known by the firm.
Become Śiva, the self turns — the turning; nectar rained as creature-life; goddess re-enters — thirteen full.

rasa.justification: The senses set like the sun; the subject finds nothing; śakti rested in Śiva and the mind dissolved — quiescence accomplished. Her play and the raining nectar are quiescence overflowing outward, not agitation returning.

sections.BOUNDARY: No new practice is prescribed; results are read. The return does not undo the ascent — the rain-giver stays transformed while the Goddess re-enters.
sections.EXPLANATION: Fearlessness is grounded in play: her krīḍā makes every produced change safe. Nectar-intoxication ferments many births' stained residue until she shakes the stained souls off the snare — stage-arrival enacted. Transmission signs its body (the Timirodghāṭana list: thrill, tears, yawning, faltering voice, burst knots, throbbing drops), and the list resolves into the declared final state. Repose is double: senses set without, śakti dissolved in the supreme within; the subject finds no other object. Transformation's thesis sentence (become Śiva, the self turns) overflows as rain — divine nectar that is creature-life — and the re-entering Goddess seals thirteen.
sections.FUNCTION: Releases fear, seals repose, and bends the summit back into return — transformation raining down as nectar for creatures.
sections.KEY TERMS: krīḍā (play) — her play as the ground of fearlessness; bhūmikāgamana (stage-arrival) — the shaking-off enacted; antāvasthā (final state) — the sign-list resolved and declared; viśrāma (rest) — senses set, śakti rested in Śiva; pariṇāma (transformation) — become Śiva, the self turns; āgamana (return) — the goddess re-enters, thirteen sealed; amṛta (nectar) — creature-life rained.
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: The tenth through thirteenth members pledged at the opening are paid here to the syllable; the quoted sign-verses are stage-arrival wearing another scripture's words.
sections.RELATED: Timirodghāṭana 4.8-10 near-verbatim (sdv): the teaching's Kaula age; sṛṣṭisaṃkrānti confirmed via Timirodghāṭana 6.6.
sections.SUMMARY: Whatever the state brews, none of it is to be feared — the Goddess plays. Nectar-drunk she multiplies changes and shakes the stained souls off their snare; the body testifies with thrill, tears, yawning, faltering voice, burst knots, throbbing drops. Senses set, śakti rests in Śiva, the self turns Śiva and rains life-nectar — and the Goddess enters again: thirteen in full.
